chunks: Ali ibn Ja'far narrated from his brother Musa (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a man who designated the price of his female slave as a sacrificial offering (hady) for the Kaaba, asking what he should do. He said: 'Indeed, a man came to my father who had designated his female slave as a hady for the Kaaba, so he said to him: "Order a crier to stand at Al-Hijr and announce: O anyone whose wealth has diminished, or whose supply has been cut off, or whose food has run out, let him come to so-and-so son of so-and-so." And he ordered him to give [the slave] one by one until he had distributed the price of the female slave as charity."'

key_terms.الْحِجْر: Al-Hijr (a specific area near the Kaaba)

ai.seo_question: What is the procedure for a hady that is a female slave?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the mechanism of manumitting a slave designated as a *hady* by publicly announcing the availability of the slave to those who can afford her, ensuring the value is distributed as charity. It highlights the Shia juristic principle that the slave's freedom is achieved through the gradual spending of her market value, linking the concept of *hady* (sacrificial offering) with *manumission* (itq). This method ensures the transaction remains valid while fulfilling the religious obligation of freeing the slave for the sake of God.
